scope: Eight vehicles, two newly injected simultaneous signal-controller faults, plus the retained background hold at intersection_2_3; one fixed public demand trace and one network; deterministic native CityFlow only.
bit_mapping_note: Displayed masks are format(integer_mask, '08b'); vehicle index 0 is the least-significant/rightmost bit. The local-choice mask was recomputed with this mapping.
limitations: One fixed demand trace and one road network; no cross-network generalization.
The local-best combination is still better than all-wait; joint optimization improves it by only 27 simulated seconds.
All 256 options were exhaustively evaluated, so a deterministic solver fully solves this task.
No LLM, AIOS, multi-agent, subagent, or 20% serial/parallel speedup result.
The two target faults coexist with the retained background hold at intersection_2_3.
interpretation: The simultaneous two-intersection event creates a small but measurable difference between singleton-local choices and the exhaustive joint optimum. This is evidence of coupled effects in this one case, not evidence that multi-agent collaboration is necessary.
